settings.heading: Fly smarter, stay safer: Aviation alcohol & drug testing solutions

settings.text:
Safety in the aviation industry leaves no room for compromise.

Whether on the tarmac, in the cockpit, or behind the scenes, drug and alcohol impairment poses a serious risk to passenger safety, crew wellbeing, and operational reliability. That’s why aviation organisations across Australia enforce strict testing protocols — not just to meet compliance requirements, but to protect lives.

Andatech supports the aviation industry with Australian Standard-certified breathalysers and drug testing solutions, purpose-built for high-pressure, safety-critical environments. Our devices deliver accurate, reliable results that help uphold CASA compliance, strengthen your drug and alcohol management plan (DAMP), and maintain public trust at every level of your operations.

Alcohol and drug testing in aviation is essential for safety and regulatory compliance. Pilots, air traffic controllers, and ground crew perform critical tasks requiring full cognitive function.

Testing prevents impairment-related incidents, ensures compliance with CASA regulations, and protects passengers, crew, and equipment. Early detection of substance misuse enables timely intervention, promoting a safer, more efficient aviation workforce.

settings.heading: Managing drug and alcohol safety in aviation: Best practices for employers

settings.text:
To stay compliant with CASA and keep your crew safe, here are the key practices every aviation operator should follow:

  • Have a Drug and Alcohol Management Plan (DAMP)
  • Run training programs so your crew understands testing procedures, and how to stay safe.
  • Always conduct drug and alcohol testing as part of your pre-employment process.
  • Perform regular, unannounced drug and alcohol tests to deter use.
  • Test after any incident.
  • All testing should follow Australian standards to ensure accuracy.
  • Consult a Medical Review Officer (MRO) after positive test results.
  • Make sure your policy outlines exactly what happens if someone tests positive.
  • All drug and alcohol testing results must be handled discreetly.

settings.heading: Who can be tested under a CASA-approved DAMP?

settings.text:
Anyone that performs or is eligible to perform a safety sensitive aviation activity. This includes but is not limited to:

  • Flight crew
  • Ground handlers
  • Cabin crew
  • refuellers
  • Aviation security staff
  • Aircraft dispatchers
  • Maintenance personnel

settings.heading: What is the legal alcohol limit for aviation employees in Australia?
settings.text: If a person tests positive during an alcohol breath test, a second test will be administered. If the test subject records a BAC of .02 or higher, they will be immediately removed from duty.

settings.heading: How often should aviation employees be tested for drugs and alcohol?
settings.text:
Testing frequency is determined by the organisation's DAMP. Employers can conduct tests:

  • Pre-employment.
  • Random testing.
  • Post-incident testing.
  • Reasonable suspicion.
  • After an employee has tested positive and is returning to work.​

These measures ensure ongoing compliance and safety within the aviation industry.

settings.heading: How should employers test for drugs and alcohol in people performing safety sensitive aviation activities?
settings.text:
CASA guidelines indicate that alcohol testing should only be done via breath testing, whereas drug testing is recommended to be done via oral testing or saliva testing.

Urine testing is still a viable option in conduction drug testing.

settings.heading: Can an employee refuse a drug test in aviation?
settings.text:
An employee cannot be forced to conduct a drug or alcohol test. However, if they refuse, they must be removed from doing any SSAA immediately.

Failure to do so can result in a criminal charge.
